rules: Any liquid asset: stock, crypto, or leveraged/inverse ETF
Rotate each 6:30am CT run — sell yesterday, buy today's best
Leverage matched to conviction; asymmetric payoff preferred
Hard stop at entry; spot-crypto-only on weekends

positions.name: ProShares Ultra Bloomberg Crude Oil
positions.catalyst: Trump declared the US-Iran ceasefire 'over' overnight — new US strikes on Iran, revoked the waiver allowing Iranian oil sales, and renewed Strait of Hormuz disruption fears. WTI +6% to ~$74.79, Brent +6% to ~$78.66. Equities risk-off (SPY -0.8%, QQQ -1.0% pre-market). UCO (2x WTI) +4.1% pre-market to $36.04 from $34.61 close.
positions.driver: 2x long crude isolates the single clean catalyst on the tape — a hard oil supply shock from a potential Hormuz disruption — without the broad-equity beta dragging on energy-equity ETFs (ERX/GUSH) on a day when SPY/QQQ are down ~1%. Asymmetric: an escalating supply shock can keep crude running while the 8% stop bounds downside. Entered at +4.1% pre-market, well below the 8-10% no-chase threshold, so not chasing the gap. Chose UCO over ERX/GUSH (equity drag on risk-off tape) and over inverse-equity SOXS/SQQQ (SOXS already +8%, and shorting semis is a less direct expression of the oil catalyst).
positions.risks: Geopolitics is headline-driven and can reverse violently — a de-escalation or ceasefire-restored headline would send crude sharply lower, and 2x doubles that drawdown. Oil spikes on war fears often fade if no actual Hormuz closure materializes. 2x crude ETFs also carry contango decay (negligible over a 24h hold). Hard 8% stop at $33.16 bounds the leverage.
